transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because I’ve been worrying more than I think is reasonable. I mean, I know everyone worries, especially in real estate, but lately it feels like it’s about everything—clients, the market, my family, money… even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. It just seems a bit out of proportion to what’s actually happening, if that makes sense.
Do you find that this worrying happens even when you’re not around other people or in social situations?

Yes… I think it does. It’s not only when I’m around people or dealing with clients. Even when I’m home by myself, I’ll find myself going over things in my head—work, the market, my family, money, whether the condo move was the right choice. I know some of that is normal, but it just feels like I’m making everything bigger than it really is.
Do you feel like you’re able to control these worries, or does it feel like they take over even when you try to stop thinking about them?

I’d like to say I can control them, and sometimes I can talk myself down a little. But… honestly, a lot of the time they do sort of take over. I’ll tell myself, “Parin, this isn’t urgent,” and then one concern leads to another. Before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour replaying some small detail I meant to just let go. It feels a bit silly saying it out loud, but that’s what happens.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like restlessness, trouble relaxing, or muscle tension, that seem to go along with these worries?

A little, yes. I don’t want to make too much of it, but by the end of the day my neck and shoulders can feel really tight, like I’ve been bracing myself without noticing. And sometimes I catch myself clenching my jaw when I’m driving between listings or sitting at my desk. I suppose that could be related, right?
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even if just for periods of time?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I have off days like anyone, where I feel tired or a bit discouraged, but I wouldn’t say I feel hopeless. And I still enjoy the things I usually enjoy… maybe I just get distracted by worrying sometimes. Does that make sense?

Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly, maybe with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, or feeling like you’re losing control?

I don’t think so… not in that sudden, out-of-nowhere way you’re describing. I can feel worked up when I’m worried, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had an episode where it suddenly peaks like that or where I feel like I’m losing control. At least, not that I’ve noticed. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Would you say that you feel anxious or worried most days, and that it’s been happening like that for several months now?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it has been most days. It’s been going on for about a year and a couple of months now, really since after I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo. I kept thinking it would settle down once I got used to the change, but it’s sort of lingered.
Have you noticed that you have trouble concentrating because your mind is preoccupied with worries?

Yes… a little. I mean, I still get my work done, so I don’t want to overstate it, but I notice it sometimes when I’m reviewing purchase agreements or inspection addendums. I’ll read the same paragraph three or four times because some worry pops into my head and then I realize I’ve lost the thread of what I was checking. It’s frustrating, but I do catch myself and go back over it.
Have you noticed yourself getting more irritable or easily annoyed, especially when you're feeling worried or stressed?

I’m not sure I’d say more irritable, exactly. I mean, I try not to take things out on people. Maybe I get a little shorter in my head when I’m stressed, but I don’t think it comes out much. My family might notice more than I do, I suppose… but I haven’t really thought of it as a big problem. Does that make sense?
Have you had trouble sleeping because you're worrying, like difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up feeling restless?

Yes… I do have some trouble with that. I usually get into bed at a decent hour, so it’s not like I’m staying up on purpose, but then my mind starts going—condo fees, what showings I have the next day, whether I missed something in a contract. It can take me quite a while to settle down. And then in the morning I sometimes feel like I slept, but didn’t really rest, if that makes sense.
Would you say that your excessive worrying about different things has occurred on more days than not over the past six months or longer?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s probably been more days than not. It started after I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo, so… about a year and two months now, I guess.
Do you feel that your level of worry is clearly more intense or persistent than the situation around the condo move and other stressors would normally justify?

Yes… I think that’s fair to say. I mean, the condo move was a big change, so I keep telling myself it’s normal to think about it. But it’s not just that anymore. I seem to worry about clients, the market, my family, money… even whether I made the right decision moving. And when I step back, nothing terrible is actually happening most of the time, so it does feel a little out of proportion. I don’t know if that’s the right way to put it.
